title: Reload one day of a Delta table with replaceWhere
objective_text: Replace one business day of a Delta table with a corrected file using an overwrite with replaceWhere, so that day's rows are exactly the file's, every other day is untouched, and a rerun changes nothing.
scenario: silver.daily_sales is loaded one business day at a time. The source has sent a corrected file for one day: it holds that whole day as it should be, with an amount fixed, a voided sale gone and a missed sale added. Today's job appends it, so the day is loaded twice. Reload just that day.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: Delta tables silver.daily_sales (three business days) and bronze.sales_correction (one corrected day, with the date it was received) in the exercise folder, and an appending job as answer.py.
required: The corrected day in silver.daily_sales holds exactly the file's rows: the fixed amount, no voided sale, and the missed sale.
Every other day is exactly as it was.
The table keeps its four columns; received_date isn't one of them.
Running the job again leaves the table the same.

expected.description: silver.daily_sales has 8 rows: days 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-03 unchanged, and 2026-03-02 as sales 4 (15.50), 5 and 9.

verifies: After your job runs, silver.daily_sales holds the corrected day exactly as the file has it and every other day unchanged, on the exercise data and on data you haven't seen, on this PC.
sale_id is unique and never empty, the columns and types are kept, and a second run leaves the table the same.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark, in a Fabric notebook or on a Fabric lakehouse: the overwrite runs on delta-rs, and the replaceWhere check is the Academy's own, made before the write. It uses Delta's error name, but the message is worded differently from Spark's.
How the table is laid out: partitionBy does nothing here, so whether the day is a partition, how many files the overwrite rewrites, and V-Order aren't checked.
Correction files that span several days, or that arrive while another job writes the same table.

validation.pass: silver.daily_sales holds the corrected day and every other day as it was.
validation.fail: silver.daily_sales doesn't match: compare each day's rows with what it held before, and the corrected day with the file.

validation.pass: The reload also works on data you haven't seen.
validation.fail: The reload doesn't hold on other data: avoid relying on this file's exact day or rows.

validation.pass: The columns, types and keys are right.
validation.fail: A column, a type or a key is off: see the detail.

validation.pass: A second run leaves silver.daily_sales the same.
validation.fail: A second run changed silver.daily_sales: look at what the write does to rows that are already there.

hints: The file is the whole day as it should be, so this is a replace, not an upsert: a sale that was voided must disappear. Which write mode replaces rows?
A plain overwrite replaces the whole table. Delta's replaceWhere option limits an overwrite to the rows that match a condition, and every row you write must match it too.
Build the condition from the file's own business day (sale_date, not when the file was received), and use mode("overwrite") with .option("replaceWhere", ...).
explanation: When a source resends a complete slice of a table, such as one business day, the safe reload replaces exactly that slice. An overwrite with replaceWhere does it in one commit: it removes the rows that match the condition and writes the new ones, so other days are untouched and a rerun leaves the same rows. Delta also checks that every row written matches the condition, which catches a condition built from the wrong column or the wrong day before anything changes. A plain overwrite replaces the whole table, an append loads the day twice, a MERGE by key keeps a sale the source voided, and a condition wider than the file's day deletes days the file doesn't hold.
troubleshooting: Only the corrected day is left: the overwrite has no replaceWhere, so it replaced the whole table.
The day appears twice, and once more on every run: the write appends; replaceWhere only applies to an overwrite.
DELTA_REPLACE_WHERE_MISMATCH: the rows written don't match the condition. Check which date column and which day it names.
A later day disappeared: the condition matches more than the file's day.
A voided sale is still there: an upsert keeps rows the file no longer has; replace the day instead.
reset: Reset rebuilds silver.daily_sales and bronze.sales_correction from setup.sql and puts the appending job back.
review_notes: replaceWhere runs in the learner shim through spark_replace_where.py (PR #3029): an overwrite replaces only matching rows, a row outside the condition raises DELTA_REPLACE_WHERE_MISMATCH and writes nothing, and an append ignores it with a note, as in Delta.
wrong-append-with-replace-where shows that last rule: the option is set but the append still doubles the day.
The solution reads the day from the file and asserts it holds one day; the hidden data corrects a different day, so a typed-in date fails there.
